title: HTTPS protects the connection
summary: HTTPS uses TLS to encrypt traffic between the browser and server. A certificate identifies the hostname for that connection.
introduction: HTTPS uses TLS to encrypt traffic between the browser and server. A certificate identifies the hostname for that connection. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: HTTPS uses TLS to encrypt traffic between the browser and server. A certificate identifies the hostname for that connection.

blocks.code:
Browser -> encrypted HTTPS connection -> server
Certificate: must match the intended hostname
Keys: kept private on the server side
blocks.title: HTTPS protects the connection

blocks.text: Encryption protects the connection. It does not prove that the site's content is honest or bug-free.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain why a private key must never be shipped as a public asset.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not copy a real private key into a tutorial or public repository.
For more detail later, use this [Nginx further reading](https://nginx.org/en/docs/beginners_guide.html).

seo.title: Nginx: HTTPS protects the connection
seo.description: Learn about https protects the connection in Nginx. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
